user.title: SLEMS system
user.description: Select the device of your smart meter and those of your PV systems: SLEMS suggests their sensors in the next step, you check and correct them. The devices that fit best come first; what you entered in the energy dashboard of Home Assistant is preselected. Leave empty to choose the sensors by hand.

data_description.grid_device: The device that measures the power at the grid connection point, e.g. a Shelly Pro 3EM, a Tibber Pulse or the meter at a SolarEdge inverter.
data_description.pv_devices: One or several, e.g. the inverter on the roof and the one of a balcony system. Their power is summed up.

system.title: SLEMS system
system.description: Select the measurements of your energy system. Batteries are added afterwards on the integration page. Right now the grid power shows {grid_now} and the PV {pv_now}. Export must be negative; if it is positive, turn on **Invert grid power sign**.

data.grid_modbus: Also read the smart meter over Modbus

data_description.grid_power_entity: Power at the grid connection point. Expected sign: positive = import, negative = export.
data_description.grid_power_inverted: Enable if your meter reports export as positive.
data_description.pv_power_entity: Current PV production. Used for the energy flow and the house consumption balance. Several PV systems are summed up.
data_description.weather_entity: Optional. Improves the consumption forecast (e.g. heat pump demand).
data_description.pv_forecast_entries: Solar forecast integrations (e.g. Forecast.Solar, Solcast). Several entries, e.g. one per roof plane, are summed up.
data_description.outdoor_temperature_entity: Optional. Temperature sensor with history for the heat pump forecast. Without it, SLEMS records the temperature of the weather entity itself.
data_description.house_history_entity: Optional. Power sensor of the house consumption with existing history (e.g. from another integration). Used for the time before SLEMS recorded its own values.
data_description.grid_power_l1_entity: Optional, together with L2 and L3: the power of each phase at the grid connection point, with the same sign as the grid power. SLEMS then learns the phase of every battery and consumer behind the smart meter (sensor **Phase**) and reports when it changes.
data_description.grid_modbus: Optional. Reads the grid power directly from a SunSpec meter (e.g. at a SolarEdge inverter, through a Modbus proxy) every fraction of a second. The control sees each value sooner than through the entity; the entity stays the fallback and the history.
data_description.grid_import_energy_entity: Optional. Energy counter of the smart meter for the import (kWh). Used for tariffs and bills; without it SLEMS uses the hourly mean of the grid power, which nets import and export within an hour.
data_description.grid_export_energy_entity: Optional. Energy counter of the smart meter for the export (kWh).

grid_modbus.title: Smart meter over Modbus
grid_modbus.description: Connects through the shared Modbus connection of Home Assistant. If the inverter integration keeps the inverter's only Modbus connection to itself, enter the Modbus proxy in front of it. SLEMS finds the meter in the SunSpec model chain.

data_description.grid_modbus_interval_s: 0.5 s is enough for the control; shorter puts more load on the connection.
data_description.grid_modbus_sign: Automatic: SLEMS compares a few values with the grid power entity (needs some import or export).

grid_meter.title: Choose the meter
grid_meter.description: The inverter lists several meters. Choose the meter at the grid connection point; the current power helps to recognise it.

error.no_sunspec: The device reports no SunSpec model chain (register 40000, 0 or 50000).
error.no_meter: The SunSpec model chain contains no meter (model 201 to 204).
error.sign_undecidable: The grid power is too small to compare the sign (Modbus {modbus} W, entity {entity} W). Try again later or choose the sign.
error.sign_mismatch: Modbus ({modbus} W) and entity ({entity} W) match with neither sign. Is the right meter chosen? Otherwise choose the sign.
error.pv_is_own_pv: These entities are the own PV modules or the output of a battery: {own_pv}. SLEMS counts their production with the battery; as a PV system it would count twice. Remove them from **PV power**.

search.title: Marstek Venus in the network
search.description: {count} battery/batteries found (state of charge in brackets). Batteries already added and batteries whose Modbus connection is held by another integration are not listed.

marstek_venus_e3.title: Marstek Venus E 3.0
marstek_venus_e3.description: Connection via Modbus TCP (LAN). The battery accepts only one Modbus connection: do not run another integration on the same battery at the same time.

data.name: Name
data.release_state: State when SLEMS releases the battery

data_description.skip_connection_test: Save without testing the connection, e.g. while another integration still holds the Modbus connection.
data_description.efficiency_mode: Battery counters (recommended): from the lifetime charge and discharge counters of the battery; accurate at once, because the battery counts its whole operating time. Learned: from the battery power measured by SLEMS; needs about three full charge cycles first. Manual: fixed value.
data_description.round_trip_efficiency_pct: Energy out / energy in (AC). Fixed value in manual mode, otherwise used until enough data has been measured.
data_description.release_state: Automatic: the battery's own logic takes over again (e.g. its zero export). Standby: the battery stays idle at 0 W until something else takes it over. Applies when SLEMS stops controlling it, e.g. in operating mode Off, without smart meter values or when the battery is removed from SLEMS.
data_description.purchase_price_eur: Optional, with the rated cycles: for the wear costs per kWh (price ÷ (cycles × usable capacity)) used by price aware actions that cost a cycle, e.g. charging from the grid. 0: no wear costs (home storage systems age mostly with time, temperature and state of charge, often before their rated cycles are used up). Without it SLEMS assumes a low estimate of 1 ct/kWh.
data_description.rated_cycles: Optional: full cycles according to the manufacturer (e.g. from the data sheet or warranty).
data_description.self_test_on_setup: Recommended: SLEMS charges and discharges the battery with little power for a few minutes and checks whether smart meter and readings match (sign, units, counters, state of charge). It starts as soon as SLEMS is in operating mode **Active**; the result appears as a notification.

ha_device.title: Battery from existing entities
ha_device.description: Select the device of the battery in Home Assistant: SLEMS suggests its entities in the next steps, also from the energy dashboard, you check and correct them. The devices that fit best come first; the battery of a hybrid inverter you set up as a PV system, or one of the energy dashboard, is preselected. Leave empty to choose all entities by hand.

ha_entities.title: Battery from existing entities
ha_entities.description: Entities suggested from the device are filled in; check them. Only read-only: SLEMS never sends commands (e.g. while another integration controls the battery). Controlled: switch off the battery's own control logic (e.g. zero export) in its integration, otherwise both control at the same time.

data.name: Name
data.own_pv: Own PV modules at the battery

data_description.power_entity: Required when SLEMS controls the battery: it is part of the power available for control. With **Own PV modules at the battery** optional: SLEMS uses own PV − output.
data_description.power_inverted: SLEMS expects positive = charging. Enable if the sensor reports discharging as positive.
data_description.own_pv: Enable for a battery whose PV modules feed the house only through the battery's output (plug-in battery such as Marstek B2500 or Zendure SolarFlow, hybrid inverter). Their production counts as PV; do not enter them as a PV system as well.
data_description.battery_control: Set point: one number entity with the signed power. Separate: one number for charging and one for discharging, optionally a mode select. Script: a script receives the power as variable power_w (+charge / -discharge). Output: one number with the output into the house, only with **Own PV modules at the battery**.
data_description.battery_temperature_entity: Optional: enables the temperature charge limit.
data_description.max_cell_voltage_entity: Optional, together with the lowest cell voltage: gentle charging near the top, cell delta and cell balancing (LFP cells).
data_description.charged_energy_entity: Optional, together with the discharged energy: efficiency from the battery counters.

ha_own_pv.title: Own PV modules
ha_own_pv.description: SLEMS counts the modules as PV and the battery power as own PV + input − output. Without an input from the grid the battery charges only from its modules; it discharges at most the highest output minus the own PV, and PV above the highest output charges it in any case.

data.own_pv_entity: Power of the own PV modules
data.passes_pv_through: Passes the PV through when full
data.remove_from_pv: Remove them from the PV systems

data_description.own_pv_entity: Power of the modules at the battery's PV inputs (DC, e.g. "Total input").
data_description.output_entity: Power the unit feeds into the house (AC, positive while feeding).
data_description.input_entity: Power the unit takes from the grid to charge (AC, positive while charging). Required for an input set point.
data_description.max_output_w: Limit of the inverter at the output, e.g. 800 W; own PV and discharge share it.
data_description.passes_pv_through: When full the device feeds its PV into the house whatever the output set point. Otherwise SLEMS raises the output in small steps at the top of the charge, so the device does not curtail its modules.
data_description.own_pv_forecast_entry: Forecast entry of these modules. It counts towards the PV forecast of the installation; without it the battery does not charge in the forecast of the state of charge.
data_description.remove_from_pv: On saving SLEMS removes them from the PV systems of the system settings.

ha_output.title: Control by output
ha_output.description: SLEMS turns the battery power into an output: output = own PV − charge power, between 0 and the highest output. With an input it charges beyond the own PV from the grid (input = charge power − own PV, output 0). With the release state **Standby** input and output stay at 0 W: the battery charges from its modules only.

data_description.output_setpoint_entity: Number entity with the output into the house. It must not be stored permanently by the device (flash wear with frequent set points).
data_description.input_setpoint_entity: Number entity with the charge power from the grid (e.g. **inputLimit** of Zendure). It must not be stored permanently by the device either.
data_description.mode_entity: Select that switches between charging from the grid and feeding into the house (e.g. **acMode** of Zendure); the options are assigned in the next step.
data_description.remote_entity: Switch or select that puts the battery under external control. SLEMS switches it on before the first set point and off when it releases the battery to **Automatic**.

data_description.setpoint_inverted: SLEMS writes positive = charging. Enable if the entity expects discharging as positive.
data_description.remote_entity: Switch or select that puts the battery under external control (e.g. **Manual battery control** of Omnibattery). SLEMS switches it on before the first set point and off when it releases the battery to **Automatic**, so the battery controls itself again (e.g. its zero export). Without it, **Automatic** is only possible with a mode option for automatic; leave it empty if you switch it yourself and choose **Standby** when released.

ha_split.title: Control by charge and discharge power

data_description.mode_entity: Select that switches between charging, discharging and standby (e.g. a force mode); the options are assigned in the next step.
data_description.remote_entity: Switch or select that puts the battery under external control (e.g. **Manual battery control** of Omnibattery). SLEMS switches it on before the first set point and off when it releases the battery to **Automatic**, so the battery controls itself again (e.g. its zero export). Without it, **Automatic** is only possible with a mode option for automatic; leave it empty if you switch it yourself and choose **Standby** when released.

ha_script.title: Control by script
ha_script.description: The power script is started with every set point and receives the variable power_w (W, +charge / -discharge, 0 = standby).

data_description.release_script: Hands the battery back to its own logic (release state Automatic).

ha_options.title: Options of the selects
ha_options.description: Which option means what. Options left empty are not used.

data.release_state: State when SLEMS releases the battery

data_description.efficiency_mode: Battery counters: from the total charged and discharged energy. Learned (recommended without counters): from the measured battery power; needs about three full charge cycles, until then the start value is used. Manual: fixed value.
data_description.round_trip_efficiency_pct: Energy out / energy in (AC). Fixed value in manual mode, otherwise used until enough data has been measured.
data_description.release_state: Automatic: the battery's own logic takes over again (e.g. its zero export). Standby: the battery stays idle at 0 W until something else takes it over. Applies when SLEMS stops controlling it, e.g. in operating mode Off, without smart meter values or when the battery is removed from SLEMS.
data_description.min_command_interval_s: For integrations with a rate limit (often cloud based); 0 = no limit.
data_description.keepalive_s: Some batteries fall back to their own logic without new commands; 0 = SLEMS default (60 s).
data_description.purchase_price_eur: Optional, with the rated cycles: for the wear costs per kWh (price ÷ (cycles × usable capacity)) used by price aware actions that cost a cycle, e.g. charging from the grid. 0: no wear costs (home storage systems age mostly with time, temperature and state of charge, often before their rated cycles are used up). Without it SLEMS assumes a low estimate of 1 ct/kWh.
data_description.rated_cycles: Optional: full cycles according to the manufacturer (e.g. from the data sheet or warranty).
data_description.self_test_on_setup: Recommended: SLEMS charges and discharges the battery with little power for a few minutes and checks whether smart meter and readings match (sign, units, counters, state of charge). It starts as soon as SLEMS is in operating mode **Active**; the result appears as a notification.

error.no_auto_release: Automatic needs a remote control entity, a mode option for automatic or a release script; otherwise choose standby.
error.none_found: No Marstek Venus found in the network. Enter the address by hand (see README: finding the IP address); stop other integrations using the battery first.
error.output_needs_own_pv: **Output** needs **Own PV modules at the battery**.
error.input_needs_sensor: An input set point needs the **Input from the grid** in the previous step.
error.own_pv_counted_twice: These entities are also entered as PV systems: {pv_systems}. Their production would count twice. Select **Remove them from the PV systems** or choose other entities.
error.power_required: SLEMS needs the battery power to control the battery.

user.title: Consumer
user.description: Select the type and, if it is in Home Assistant, the device of the consumer: SLEMS suggests its entities in the next steps, you check and correct them. The devices that fit best come first. Leave the device empty to choose all entities by hand.

data_description.consumer_type: Heat pump consumption is forecast from the weather; a heating rod is typically used for hot water in summer. A wallbox is never part of the house consumption forecast; the next step defaults to current control, 6–16 A and 5 minutes minimum runtime and pause, and its battery support to automatic.
data_description.device: The consumer itself, e.g. the heat pump, the heating rod or the wallbox. Devices whose entities SLEMS already uses elsewhere are not listed.
data_description.meter_device: Optional, if another device measures the consumer's power and energy, e.g. a smart plug or a meter in the distribution board. Leave empty if the device measures them itself.

consumer.title: Consumer
consumer.description: Every consumer needs its own power and energy sensor. The suggestions come from the selected devices; check them.

data_description.power_entity: Its electrical power; for a heat pump not the heat output.
data_description.energy_entity: Its meter reading. If the device has none (e.g. a my-PV device in the my-PV integration of Home Assistant), create an **Integral** helper from its power sensor.
data_description.included_in_meter: Enable if the consumer is behind the smart meter, i.e. its consumption is already part of the measured grid power.
data_description.show_in_flow: Shows the consumer as its own box in the energy flow of the dashboard. Off: its consumption still counts in the house; the consumer card shows it.
data_description.hot_water: On if the heat pump also heats the hot water. SLEMS then asks for its operating mode (with **Release**) and the temperature of the storage.
data_description.control_mode: **Release**: SLEMS switches nothing itself but provides the binary sensor **Release** (on when SLEMS would switch the consumer on now; attribute **forced** from the latest start of the daily target on) and the sensor **Latest start**; an automation of your own starts the device. For a heat pump that heats a hot water storage the release is for its hot water charge: only what it draws in hot water mode is controlled, the heating stays uncontrolled.

data_description.control_entity: Switch for on/off consumers, number entity in W for power controlled ones, in A for current controlled ones (e.g. the charging current of a wallbox); with current control also a select with ampere options (e.g. **Max. charging current** of an evcc loadpoint in ha-evcc). Turn off the device's own surplus control (e.g. **Auto control** of a my-PV ELWA 2), otherwise it works against SLEMS.
data_description.nominal_power_w: A rough estimate is enough if **Use learned values** is on: SLEMS then measures the real power while it runs the consumer (operating mode active) and uses it after about 15 minutes of running (the median of its last hour of running). Rather estimate a little too low than too high: too high, SLEMS waits for a larger surplus and may never switch the consumer on, so nothing is learned. For a heat pump with **Release**: its power for hot water; SLEMS learns it in hot water mode, so it follows the coefficient of performance.
data_description.block_entity: SLEMS does not control the consumer while it is blocked (e.g. by the device or an automation): a water heater while its operation mode is "off", other entities while they are "on".
data_description.priority: 1 = highest priority when distributing surplus power.
data_description.min_on_minutes: Optional. Once switched on by SLEMS, the consumer keeps running at least this long.
data_description.min_off_minutes: Optional. Once switched off by SLEMS, the consumer stays off at least this long.
data_description.temperature_entity: Optional, e.g. the sensor of the boiler at the heating rod, or a water heater (its current temperature). SLEMS learns from the mean of the sensors how much energy the storage takes per degree and from which temperature the thermostat cycles, and plans the consumer for the feed-in cap only as far as it can still take energy.
data_description.temperature_2_entity: Optional, e.g. a sensor higher up in the boiler; makes the estimate more accurate.
data_description.min_current_a: Below this current the consumer is stopped (vehicles: usually 6 A).
data_description.phases: Phases the consumer charges with when no entity tells the active ones.
data_description.phases_entity: Optional. Sensor with the number of active phases (1 or 3), e.g. of an evcc loadpoint or a wallbox that switches phases itself; the power range follows it.
data_description.start_entity: Optional. Switch, or a select (then the options for on and off are asked next, e.g. the mode of an evcc loadpoint: now / off). Without it SLEMS stops by setting the lowest current the control entity takes (0 A if allowed); with evcc and its minimum current evcc then decides itself when to start and stop.
data_description.avoid_cycling: Start only when the forecast surplus lasts for a whole run (the minimum runtime, or what the daily target still needs if less) and keep running through dips of the surplus for up to 5 minutes (the batteries or the grid bridge them). For devices that should not be switched on and off often, e.g. with a compressor; set a minimum runtime and pause as well.
data_description.mode_entity: Entity that shows the operating mode of the heat pump (e.g. **Status** with heating, hot water, defrost); next you select the states that mean hot water.

start_options.title: Options for start and stop
start_options.description: Options of {entity} SLEMS uses to start and stop the consumer. SLEMS selects them itself; a change from outside is not taken as a request of the device and is set back while SLEMS controls the consumer.

data_description.start_on: Selected when the consumer should run. Choose the option in which the device runs without its own logic, with evcc **Fast**: with **Smart** evcc would follow the surplus itself and work against SLEMS.
data_description.start_off: Selected when the consumer should be off, with evcc **Off**.

hot_water_states.title: States for hot water
hot_water_states.description: States of {entity} (now: {state}) in which the heat pump heats hot water. Preselected is what sounds like hot water; check the selection. Only in these states its power counts as controlled.

data_description.hot_water_states: Several possible; a state that is not listed can be typed in.

error.hot_water_states_required: Select at least one state for hot water.

user.title: Add tariff
user.description: Enter the tariff line by line, or paste it as YAML (an export of SLEMS or the answer of an AI, see the README).

template_energy.title: Energy
template_energy.description:
The energy tariff of your supplier.

**Left empty, OK goes on to the grid and the levies.** You then add the prices of your energy tariff with **Add line**.

A feed-in tariff (**Feed-in · …**) always becomes a tariff of its own, next to your import tariff.

Templates contain public list prices; compare the tariff with a bill afterwards.

Your tariff is missing? Go back and paste it as YAML, e.g. made from your bill with the help of an AI: [guide]({prompt_url}).

template_rest.title: Grid and levies
template_rest.description: Preselected: the grid tariff usually combined with the energy tariff (households) and the levies of the country, each as in effect today. Change them if your grid area is a different one.

template_options.title: Options
template_options.description: Options of the chosen templates as on the price sheet, e.g. an upgrade to green electricity or a bonus with conditions (online bill, direct debit, contract term). Choose those of your contract.

elcom.title: Tariff from ElCom
elcom.description: SLEMS queries the open data of the Federal Electricity Commission ElCom (ld.admin.ch) for the tariff of your municipality: energy, grid and levies of your grid operator, excluding VAT, as the mean of the consumption category. Later years are offered as new prices once published (in September), if fetching market prices is switched on.

elcom_pick.title: Municipality and grid operator
elcom_pick.description: Choose your municipality and its grid operator.

import_yaml.title: Paste tariff as YAML
import_yaml.description: Paste the whole file (format slems-tariff, version {version} or older). Prices are net; afterwards you check name, role and VAT and can compare the tariff with a bill.

details.title: Tariff
details.description: Enter the tariff as it appears on your bill: first name, role and VAT, then the lines one by one. Consumption and feed-in are two sides of the same tariff. Enter the prices of the items net (without VAT); SLEMS adds the VAT with these rates. If your bill only shows gross prices, enter them and set the VAT to 0 %.

data_description.role: Current: what you pay now. Several current tariffs (e.g. separate contracts for import and feed-in) count together as one. Comparison: e.g. a dynamic tariff; a comparison tariff with items for only one side takes the other side from the current tariffs.

data.name: Name (as on the bill)
data.factor_pct: Share on top of the market price

data_description.unit: Spot price and monthly market price use the market prices of the **Price source** in the SLEMS settings (group **Prices**); **Fetch market prices** must be on.
data_description.price: Net (without VAT) in {minor}/kWh or {major} per year, as on the bill; a discount is negative. On the feed-in side the energy price is the credit you get. For spot price and monthly market price: the fixed markup in {minor}/kWh (negative: deduction). Percent of the group: e.g. 7 for a levy of 7 % on the other items of the same side and group.
data_description.factor_pct: Only for spot price and monthly market price: price = market price + percent of its amount + price; a markup stays a markup at a negative market price. E.g. −10 % for a credit of 90 % of the market price.
data_description.month_prices: Optional, only for the monthly market price: published values in {minor}/kWh, e.g. "2026-01: 8.5; 2026-02: 7.9". Months without a value: mean of the spot prices weighted by your feed-in.
data_description.market: Only for the monthly market price: the official monthly value the price follows. It is fetched with the market prices; until a month is published, the day-ahead mean weighted by your feed-in stands in.
data_description.max_market_ct: Optional, only for spot price and monthly market price: the market price counts at most this much in {minor}/kWh net, before the markups, e.g. 60 for a price cap of the contract. Empty: no cap.
data_description.zero_when_negative: On: the item is 0 in hours or quarter hours with a negative day-ahead price, e.g. the German EEG feed-in credit of plants since 25 February 2025. Needs **Fetch market prices**.
data_description.valid_from: Optional. For a price change: add the line again with the new price and this date.
data_description.valid_to: Optional: the last day of the line, e.g. when a price level ends.
data_description.months: Optional, e.g. for a reduced summer price.
data_description.time_from: Optional, with "Only until": a time window of the day (local time), e.g. a reduced grid price at noon. A line with a window replaces the line of the same name in its window.

check.title: Check against a bill
check.description: SLEMS computes the period of a bill with the tariff and your recorded grid import and export and shows the difference to the bill.

data.import_amount: Amount of the consumption bill (incl. VAT)
data.export_amount: Credit of the feed-in bill (incl. VAT)

export_yaml.title: Tariff as YAML
export_yaml.description: Copy the text to save the tariff or to use it in another SLEMS. Before you share it (e.g. as a template), remove personal discounts. Nothing is changed here.

update_choose.title: New prices
update_choose.description: For {template} there are corrected or newer prices or successors. Choose the one your contract follows, or none of them (then they are not offered again until something newer comes). A correction keeps the dates and also applies to the past; lines you changed yourself stay.

update_confirm.title: Take over new prices
update_confirm.description:
The current lines end the day before, the new ones apply from {date}; the old prices stay for the past (bill check, tariff comparison). Own lines stay as they are.

battery_not_responding.title: {name} does not respond
battery_not_responding.description: {name} does not deliver the power SLEMS commands (or does not confirm the commands). It was handed back to its own logic and is retried every 5 minutes; the other batteries take over. Check the connection and the battery (e.g. in the Marstek app). This message disappears when the battery delivers again.

battery_unreadable.title: {name} cannot be read
battery_unreadable.description: SLEMS has not been able to read {name} for more than 5 minutes. The battery is not planned with or controlled meanwhile. Check the network connection, the Modbus settings and whether another integration (e.g. Omnibattery) uses the only Modbus connection of the battery.

house_power_inaccurate.title: House consumption inaccurate without {name}
house_power_inaccurate.description: {name} is disabled and released to its own logic (**Automatic**), but SLEMS cannot read it. It may charge or discharge meanwhile; SLEMS counts it with 0 W, so the house consumption, the base load and what SLEMS learns from them can be off by its power. The control at the smart meter is not affected. Check the connection of the battery or set its release state to **Standby**.

grid_meter_stale.title: Smart meter does not report
grid_meter_stale.description: The smart meter entity has not reported for a while. SLEMS handed the batteries back to their own logic and controls again as soon as the meter reports. Check the smart meter and its integration.

grid_modbus_unavailable.title: Smart meter over Modbus not reachable
grid_modbus_unavailable.description: SLEMS cannot read the grid power over Modbus ({error}) and uses the smart meter entity meanwhile. Check the connection, the proxy and the settings in the options.

battery_release_failed.title: {name} could not be released
battery_release_failed.description: SLEMS could not hand {name} back to its own logic, e.g. because the connection is interrupted. The battery may still run with the last set point. SLEMS keeps trying; check the connection or the battery (e.g. in its app).

tariff_update.title: New prices for {name}
tariff_update.description: The templates of the tariff {name} have new prices from {date}. Take them over: Settings → Devices & services → SLEMS → the tariff → ⋮ → Reconfigure → Update to the new prices. The old prices stay for the past.

tariff_expired.title: {name} is no longer valid
tariff_expired.description: The prices of the tariff {name} were valid until {date}. Enter the new prices (Settings → Devices & services → SLEMS → the tariff → ⋮ → Reconfigure), e.g. as lines with "valid from", or add the new tariff.

tariff_successor.title: Successor for {name}
tariff_successor.description: The tariff {name} has a successor from {date}: {successors}. Take it over: Settings → Devices & services → SLEMS → the tariff → ⋮ → Reconfigure → Update to the new prices. The old prices stay for the past.

tariff_correction.title: Corrected prices for {name}
tariff_correction.description: A template of the tariff {name} was corrected (prices from {date}). Take it over: Settings → Devices & services → SLEMS → the tariff → ⋮ → Reconfigure → Update to the new prices. Lines you changed yourself stay.

market_price_currency.title: Market prices only in euro
market_price_currency.description: At the moment SLEMS only supports market prices in euro; Home Assistant is set to {currency}. Your tariff **{name}** follows the market price. SLEMS keeps controlling by cheap and expensive times, but does not convert the market prices (price chart, weighing against the wear costs). The tariff comparison and **Check against a bill** do not compute this tariff.

consumers_exceed_house.title: Consumers do not match the house consumption
consumers_exceed_house.description: For more than 15 minutes the consumers behind the smart meter reported more power together than the whole house: last {consumers} W at a house consumption of {house} W (from grid, PV and batteries). That is not possible. Either a consumer measures wrong (e.g. a fixed or stuck value), or it is not behind the smart meter; then switch off **Included in smart meter** in its settings. Consumers drawing power: {names}. Until this is fixed, base load and consumption forecast are wrong. The notice disappears as soon as the values match again.

grid_counters_not_netted.title: Energy counters of the smart meter do not net the phases
grid_counters_not_netted.description: The import and the export counter of the smart meter both ran in several quarter hours while the grid power showed less: they count per phase, while your utility meter usually nets the phases (in Germany and Austria). Tariffs and bills of SLEMS would then count energy that never crossed the meter. For a Shelly Pro 3EM the Shelly Phase Netting integration provides netted counters (learn more); with other meters, split the grid power into import and export with template sensors and **Integral** helpers. Or remove the counters in the SLEMS settings: SLEMS then uses its own netted values. Ignore this if your utility meter counts per phase as well.
